topics.flagship-ru-ua: Ukraine launched nearly 1,200 drones at Russian targets, one of its largest aerial attacks of the war, as US-led talks weigh European security arrangements (3 sources). The Kremlin said Europeans can join the peace talks only if they show 'readiness to contribute'. Single-outlet reports include a Ukrainian claim of a record 3,000 Russian casualties in one day, Finland saying Ukraine struck a Russian warship near its coast during the Abu Dhabi talks, and Russian drone strikes that killed several people in Ukraine overnight.
topics.flagship-ir-il: An Israeli strike on the surgery department of Nasser Hospital in Khan Younis killed at least six and wounded at least 20, according to Gaza's civil defence agency (3 sources). The US military reported downing two Iranian attack drones approaching Bahrain, while Iran's Revolutionary Guard claimed a strike on a US radar there (2 sources). Israeli shelling and drone overflights continued in southern Lebanon and over Beirut, and outlets are discussing whether Netanyahu's caretaker government could strike Iran. A single-source market-analysis piece says US nuclear use against Iran 'cannot be 100% ruled out' while noting that Trump said new military action does not seem necessary right now.
topics.T15: Coverage is sparse and mostly local or evergreen, with no major disaster standing out. Items include a Kenyan forecast of heavier-than-usual short rains linked to El Niño, an evacuation alert for Pemberton, Canada, over high river flows, and flood relief in Kogi, Nigeria. One outlet reported a nationwide FAA halt of departing flights on Friday, but the cause is not given. Several other items are insurance or preparedness pieces that appear to be old or generic.
topics.T01: The top item is Trump hinting at toppling Cuba's authorities before his term ends, calling it a failed nation (3 sources). Other reports are single-outlet: a Myanmar junta airstrike that reportedly killed two students in Mrauk-U, secretive US talks with a regime it accused of genocide that experts say may involve rare earths, and the USA withdrawing from the U17 World Cup in Qatar over armed-conflict risk.
topics.T02: Gaza's humanitarian situation is reportedly worsening amid political deadlock, with heavy rain flooding and damaging thousands of tents and several people dying (2 sources). Commentary asks whether pressure from Trump's Board of Peace on Israel and Hamas could ease conditions while peace talks are stalled.
topics.T04: The DRC Ebola outbreak continues to spread, with UN responders saying attacks by armed groups on civilians and health workers are obstructing the response (2 sources). Related single-source items say Kenya refuses to serve as an Ebola quarantine centre for foreign travelers and attribute response difficulties to US aid cuts. Other items are local or of unclear date: an unexplained illness in Rajouri, Kashmir, with 14 deaths, a cholera-linked emergency in Karaikal, a Knox County measles emergency declaration, and an old Hong Kong COVID story.
topics.T05: Stories are sparse and generic, with no acute coup signal. They cover Poland's dispute over its Constitutional Tribunal, ASEAN debating re-engagement with Myanmar's military-backed leadership with Thailand pushing for it, and Nigerian Rivers State politics after the Fubara-Wike reconciliation.
topics.T06: Violent riots were reported across Spain ahead of elections (3 sources). Single-outlet items describe renewed mass protests in France, with 70,000 police reportedly deployed, and Europe bracing for further unrest in Germany, Italy and Portugal. The coverage is largely commentary and tabloid-style, so the scale is not independently clear.
topics.T07: The UN nuclear watchdog said in a confidential report that it is 'increasingly concerned' about an Isfahan enrichment plant that Iran declared last year but has not allowed it to inspect (7 sources). Iran's Mohsen Rezaei reiterated that no enriched material will leave the country, and a clerical body is said to call NPT withdrawal a 'national demand'. Other items include a simulation of a space nuclear detonation and an unverified claim about a Japanese warning of dirty bombs, which has no source coverage.
topics.T08: Four Nagas were killed in a suspected militant ambush in Ukhrul, Manipur (3 sources), and a manhunt continues in Kulgam for an LeT-linked suspect in an attack on CRPF personnel (3 sources). Other reports cover an airstrike that killed three militants in northern Iraq, a US assessment that Nigeria is not doing enough against attacks on Christians, and fighting between JNIM and ISIL in Burkina Faso. Pakistani police reportedly foiled an explosives-laden van attack on a police station in Dera Ismail Khan.
topics.T09: No new hostage or kidnapping developments are reported. The only item is a retrospective on Evan Gershkovich's arrest by Russia's FSB and his later release in a prisoner swap.
topics.T10: Germany's parliament passed an overhaul of its intelligence agencies, giving the BND new powers for covert operations such as sabotage and cyber attacks. Trump is backing $350 billion in a reconciliation bill for the defense industry, citing 'inventory shortfalls' (2 sources). Other items include Poland's defense buildup through its state armaments group, warnings about German debt from military spending, a Swedish caretaker budget, and Hegseth's uncertain future.
topics.T11: India and Sri Lanka began the 12th Mitra Shakti joint military exercise, running November 13-26 at Maduru Oya in Sri Lanka (7 sources). It involves a 170-member Indian contingent, primarily from the Rajputana Rifles.
topics.T12: A Microsoft outage is affecting companies and governments worldwide, and the company is still trying to identify the cause and restore its servers (17 sources). Separately, Operation Endgame took down servers tied to the Gootloader, CastleRAT and StealC malware tools and seized about 6.4 million stolen logins (2 sources). Check Point reportedly issued emergency hotfixes for a zero-day flaw exploited for root access since late October.
topics.T13: Trump threatened to immediately double tariffs on Mexico if it fails to stop migrant caravans heading to the US border (3 sources). Single-outlet items cover Ethiopian mothers who fled to Kenya struggling to feed their children, migration pressure on a small Spanish island, and a Welsh Senedd speech ban over migration comments.
topics.T16: The Irish Taoiseach confirmed he will contest the next general election, and Brazil's Flávio Bolsonaro said he will run again after losing last month's presidential election. In the US, Dan Patrick conceded Texas has 'turned purple' after Democratic gains, Newsom set an early-January decision date on a 2028 run, and a GOP fundraiser reportedly warned of weak donor support for Vance. Rubio acknowledged economic strain after GOP midterm losses (4 sources). Other items are minor, including Nigeria's Makinde positioning against Tinubu.

bluf: The UN nuclear watchdog says it is 'increasingly concerned' about an Isfahan enrichment plant that Iran declared last year but has not let it inspect, according to a confidential report seen by Reuters and AP (7 sources). Separately, a Microsoft outage is hitting companies and governments worldwide, and the company is still trying to identify the cause and restore its servers (17 sources). In Gaza, an Israeli strike on the surgery department of Nasser Hospital in Khan Younis killed at least six and wounded at least 20, according to the civil defence agency (3 sources). Ukraine fired nearly 1,200 drones at Russian targets in one of its largest aerial attacks of the war while US-led talks consider European security, and the Kremlin said Europeans may join the talks only if they show 'readiness to contribute'. The Ebola outbreak in the DRC continues to spread, with UN responders saying armed-group attacks on civilians and health workers are obstructing the response (2 sources). The US military reported shooting down two Iranian attack drones approaching Bahrain without damage, while Iran's Revolutionary Guard claimed a strike on a US radar in the kingdom (2 sources). Trump also hinted at toppling Cuba's authorities before leaving office, calling Cuba a failed nation (3 sources).
